# VideoToolbox Remote (`videotoolbox_remote`) Briefing

**Version**: v0.9.18
**License**: LGPL v2.1+ by default; optional GPL components depend on FFmpeg configuration.
**Goal**: High-quality, low-power remote hardware video processing: keep Plex and automation on Linux while a macOS 13+ Mac (including macOS 27) supplies VideoToolbox over LAN.

## What It Does
VideoToolbox Remote turns an Apple Silicon or supported T2 Mac on a LAN into a hardware H.264/HEVC transcoding engine. FFmpeg clients on Linux, Windows, or macOS select remote codecs (`h264_videotoolbox_remote`, `hevc_videotoolbox_remote`). Supported Plex packet transcodes can run on GPU-less Linux hosts while the Mac performs video decode, optional resize and encode. Batch jobs, stock Linux VA-API encoding and experimental OBS live encoding use the same daemon. Published quality/CPU measurements exist; whole-system watts and energy savings are not yet measured.

## Core Architecture
- **Server (`vtremoted`)**: Swift daemon wrapping VideoToolbox. Defaults to loopback TCP 5555; explicit private/VPN bind or a tunnel is needed for other hosts.
- **Client (`ffmpeg`)**: Modified FFmpeg with custom remote codecs in `libavcodec/vtremote_*.c`.
- **OBS Plugin**: Experimental, with separate H.264/HEVC encoder entries. Raw-frame upload; composition and delivery stay in OBS. Mock/libobs coverage is not proof of every live output/shutdown path.
- **VA-API Driver**: Linux x86_64 encode-only driver for stock applications. Local software decode/filter/upload; requires a render node (physical or VGEM where available). No decode, VPP, B-frames or external DMA-BUF.
- **Plex Integration**: Separate Linux x86_64 container packet shim, not a VA-API driver path. No Linux render node. Bundled libavcodec fingerprint/version and command graphs are checked before offload; unknown builds/graphs remain native. Plex Pass and enabled hardware acceleration/encoding are required for normal claimed playback. PMS 1.43.3.10896 has unclaimed end-to-end coverage; recognized 1.43.4 SDR graphs do not imply all-path coverage.

## Three Operating Modes
1. **Remote Encode**: Raw frames (NV12/P010) in, compressed packets (H.264/HEVC) out.
2. **Remote Decode**: Compressed packets in, raw frames out.
3. **Remote Transcode**: Compressed packets in/out; supported video decode/resize/encode on Mac. Files, audio, subtitles and muxing remain local. Arbitrary video filters are not offloaded.

## Repository Structure
- `/vtremoted`: SwiftPM project (Server). `Sources/VTRemotedCore/` contains core logic.
- `/ffmpeg`: FFmpeg fork (Client). `libavcodec/vtremote_*` files implement the protocol and codecs.
- `/obs-plugin`: OBS Studio encoder plugin (C/C++).
- `/vaapi-driver`: Linux VA-API driver, probe, static C SDK, packaging, and Plex smoke tooling.
- `/docs`: Jekyll documentation site (architecture, protocol spec, guides).
- `/tests/integration`: Shell-based integration tests + Python mock server.

## Quick Start

### 1. Build Server (macOS)
```bash
cd vtremoted && swift build -c release
# Binary: .build/release/vtremoted
```

### 2. Build Client (Linux/Mac/Windows)
The FFmpeg client build requires `liblz4` and `libzstd`.
```bash
cd ffmpeg
./configure --enable-videotoolbox-remote --enable-liblz4 --enable-libzstd
make -j$(nproc)
```

### 3. Usage (Encoding)
```bash
./ffmpeg -i input.mp4 \
  -c:v h264_videotoolbox_remote \
  -vt_remote_host <MAC_IP>:5555 \
  -b:v 5M \
  output.mp4
```

## Protocol Overview (v1, Stable)
- **Transport**: TCP, persistent connection.
- **Handshake**: `HELLO` (token, codec) -> `HELLO_ACK` (status, capabilities).
- **Config**: `CONFIGURE` (resolution, fps, options) -> `CONFIGURE_ACK` (extradata/SPS/PPS).
- **Streaming**: `FRAME` (pixel data) <-> `PACKET` (encoded bytes).
- **Completion**: `FLUSH` -> remaining frames/packets -> `DONE`; fatal errors and timeouts are not successful completion.
- **Framing**: 12-byte header (magic `VTR1`, version, type, length).
- **Wire compression**: LZ4, Zstd, or none. FFmpeg/OBS default to LZ4; the VA-API driver defaults to automatic selection. The macOS server loads LZ4/Zstd at runtime only when requested.

## Performance
- Published comparisons use Big Buck Bunny and FFmpeg testsrc2/SMPTE color-bar inputs, with identical fixture hashes on both hosts.
- Pipelines are Intel iGPU VA-API, CPU fast/medium presets, local VideoToolbox and remote VideoToolbox.
- Local and remote VideoToolbox use the same M2 Mac; the remote client runs on the Intel Linux host.
- The original five-pipeline comparison was measured with v0.9.14. Big Buck Bunny H.264 local/remote VideoToolbox rows were refreshed with v0.9.16 after closing screen sharing; other valid results retain their original dates and builds. Average/VBR, zero frame reordering and a 60-frame maximum GOP are shared. Intel HEVC uses past-reference GPB B-slices despite `-bf 0`. Of 120 moving outputs, 117 meet the 2% whole-file budget target; three retained CPU-medium HEVC 720p files deviate by at most 2.066%. Static bars are separate controls.
- Interactive graphs compare transcode throughput, VMAF and submitting-process CPU time by input, codec and resolution. Exact values include measurement dates, release versions, physical file size, full reported container bitrate, SSIM and repeat ranges. All first-repeat quality measurements score all 1,800 frames with the same Linux reference/model settings; original and refreshed scorer hashes are recorded per row. JSON binds scores to their own file sizes/hashes and preserves every measured repeat. Whole-file bitrate includes container overhead and filler.
- Packet transcoding avoids raw-frame network transport when local video filters are unnecessary. Raw-frame encoding has different bandwidth costs.
- Intel RAPL package energy is not whole-system power. Whole-system watt savings have not been measured.

## Key Constraints
- Server **must** run on macOS with hardware encoding support.
- Network: wired LAN strongly recommended (1GbE minimum, 2.5GbE+ for 4K).
- No encryption by default — use SSH tunnel or VPN for untrusted networks.
- Token-based authentication is optional (for LAN environments).
- Plex tone mapping, deinterlace, subtitle burn-in and unsupported constraints are not offloaded; native paths may consume Linux CPU. Direct Play needs no remote video transcode.
- The Plex bootstrap image is digest-pinned but downloads the selected PMS runtime at startup; an unrecognized runtime upgrade can disable remote offload.

## Supported Codecs & Formats
- **Encoding**: H.264 (Baseline/Main/High), HEVC (Main, Main10)
- **Decoding**: H.264, HEVC
- **Pixel Formats**: NV12, YUV420P, P010LE, YUV420P10LE, YUV420P10BE; HEVC expanded paths also negotiate BGRA, AYUV, and P210LE where the server/runtime supports them.
- **Platforms**: macOS (server), Linux x86_64/arm64, Windows x86_64, macOS x86_64/arm64 (FFmpeg client). The Linux arm64 release requires Ubuntu 24.04-compatible shared libraries and glibc 2.39 or newer; build from source on Debian 12 / Raspberry Pi OS Bookworm. VA-API release assets remain Linux x86_64 only.
